interface.name: kde_stereo_content_manager_v1
interface.description:
A program tells the compositor that a surface's picture holds two views, one per eye, with their packing (side by side or top and bottom, full or half resolution per eye) and eye order (left or right first). The compositor renders the declared surface once per eye with that eye's view. The global being present announces support.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is a desktop environment implementation detail. Regular clients must not use this protocol. Backward incompatible changes may be added without bumping the major version of the extension.

request.name: create

description.summary: Create a stereo content declaration for a surface

request.description: Creates a kde_stereo_content_v1 object for the given surface. The declaration is none until set_content is called. If the surface already has a declaration, the already_declared error is raised.

entry.name: already_declared
entry.summary: the surface already has a stereo content declaration

interface.name: kde_stereo_content_v1

description.summary: stereo content declaration of one surface

interface.description: The declaration of one surface, created with kde_stereo_content_manager_v1.create.

entry.name: invalid_class
entry.summary: class or sub-class out of range (both are 8-bit values)

request.name: destroy
request.description: The surface's picture is ordinary again.

enum.name: content

description.summary: packing and eye order of the two views

enum.description: Same packing as HDMI's 3D structures, same eye order as the frame packing SEI: the right-first values carry the right eye's view on the left or at the top. The values match the X11 property _KDE_NET_WM_STEREO_CONTENT version 1.

entry.name: side_by_side_half
entry.summary: side by side, half width per eye, left first

entry.name: side_by_side_half_right_first
entry.summary: side by side, half width per eye, right first

entry.name: side_by_side_full
entry.summary: side by side, full width per eye, left first

entry.name: side_by_side_full_right_first
entry.summary: side by side, full width per eye, right first

entry.name: top_and_bottom_half
entry.summary: top and bottom, half height per eye, left first

entry.name: top_and_bottom_half_right_first
entry.summary: top and bottom, half height per eye, right first

entry.name: top_and_bottom_full
entry.summary: top and bottom, full height per eye, left first

entry.name: top_and_bottom_full_right_first
entry.summary: top and bottom, full height per eye, right first

request.name: set_content
request.description: Takes effect with the next commit of the surface. Declaring none has the same effect as destroying the object.

enum.name: content_class
enum.description: The kind of program the content comes from, so the compositor can choose a suggested mode per kind. The standard classes also map to wp_content_type_v1 (scientific is none there): a client that knows wp_content_type_v1 should set it too, so the output's HDMI content type follows as the compositor already does.

request.name: set_content_class

description.summary: Declare the content's class and sub-class

request.description: Takes effect with the next commit of the surface. The sub-class is per class, append-only, 0 means unspecified. For game: 1 = vr (a VR engine adapted to the display, entertainment), 2 = 3d (a game with its own stereo output), 3 = gl (stereo made by a wrapper), 4 = stereogl (OpenGL quad-buffer stereo). For video: 1 = legacy (frame-compatible broadcast and web 3D, Blu-ray 3D), 2 = current (MV-HEVC spatial video, VR180). For scientific: 1 = vr (work VR: surgery and medical training, design review, industrial training). Other values are reserved.
